When the kettle sings its copper morning
Basil leans against the open sill
Tomato vines in patient harness
The garden hums a slow green psalm
Pebble path and chipped ceramic whistle
Rain that nurses every crooked stem
A sparrow keeps the birdbath ledger
While the soil drinks the quiet rain
We pinch the mint and breathe the wet thyme
Nobody here keeps count of time

The old wheelbarrow knows a hundred seasons
Its rust a scripture only hands can read
We carry baskets like a quiet promise
And let the compost teach us all we need
